subtopics.title: From Magma to Lava — and Why Some Eruptions Explode

questions.question: The difference between magma and lava is that:
options: Magma is molten rock below the surface; lava is the same material once it reaches the surface
Magma contains no gas; lava does
Magma is solid; lava is liquid
Magma is found only at hot spots

questions.question: Basaltic magma produces effusive rather than explosive eruptions because it is:
options: Cool and high in silica, so gas is trapped
Very hot and low in silica, so it is runny and dissolved gas escapes easily
Free of all dissolved gases
Denser than the surrounding rock

questions.question: At a convergent boundary, magma is generated because:
options: Plates pull apart and reduce pressure on the mantle
A mantle plume burns through the middle of a plate
Water driven out of the descending slab lowers the melting point of the mantle above it
Friction between plates melts the crust directly

questions.question: A volcano described as DORMANT is one that:
options: Is erupting at present
Has never erupted
Is no longer supplied with magma
Has not erupted recently but is still capable of erupting

subtopics.title: The Structure of a Volcano and the Main Types

questions.question: A caldera differs from a crater in that it:
options: Is a vast basin formed when the summit collapses after an eruption empties the magma chamber
Is the small funnel-shaped opening at the top of the vent
Is always filled with lava
Forms only on shield volcanoes

questions.question: A shield volcano has gentle slopes and a very wide base because:
options: It is built entirely from loose ash
Its runny basaltic lava flows a long way before cooling
It erupts only once
Its magma chamber lies very deep

questions.question: A composite (strato) volcano is built of:
options: Solid granite formed underground
A single thick lava dome
Alternating layers of ash from explosive phases and lava from effusive phases
Loose cinders only

questions.question: Small cones built on the flanks of a volcano by side vents are called:
options: Calderas
Batholiths
Lava plateaux
Secondary or parasitic cones

questions.question: A SILL differs from a DYKE in that a sill:
options: Lies horizontally between existing rock layers, while a dyke cuts across them
Is always made of granite
Forms above the ground surface
Contains diamonds

questions.question: The flat-topped koppies of the Karoo exist because:
options: Wind has flattened their summits
A hard dolerite sill caps each hill and resists weathering better than the surrounding shale
They are extinct composite volcanoes
They were levelled by glaciers

questions.question: The Drakensberg and the Lesotho highlands are made of:
options: Folded sandstone of the Cape Supergroup
Granite of a batholith
Stacked basalt lava flows erupted from long fissures as Gondwana began breaking apart
Ash from a single composite cone

questions.question: The Bushveld Igneous Complex, holding the world's greatest platinum reserves, is an example of a:
options: Volcanic neck
Lava plateau
Cinder cone
Lopolith — a saucer-shaped intrusion

questions.question: The volcanic hazard responsible for the greatest loss of life is:
options: The pyroclastic flow — superheated gas, ash and rock racing downslope faster than anyone can run
The lava flow, which usually moves slowly enough to walk away from
The volcanic gas released between eruptions
The hot spring at the base of the cone

questions.question: A lahar is:
options: A dome of viscous lava over the vent
A volcanic mudflow formed when ash mixes with heavy rain or melted snow and races down valleys
A cloud of sulphur dioxide
A collapsed caldera floor

questions.question: Densely populated farming communities live on volcanic slopes chiefly because:
options: Volcanoes never erupt twice
Governments pay them to stay
Weathered ash and lava produce exceptionally fertile soils rich in potassium, phosphorus and magnesium
The slopes are the flattest available land

questions.question: Volcanic eruptions can be managed more successfully than earthquakes because:
options: Eruptions are far less dangerous
Volcanoes always erupt on a fixed timetable
Lava can be diverted with walls in every case
Rising magma gives measurable warning — earthquake swarms, ground swelling, increased gas emission and rising ground temperature

questions.question: In the cooldrink comparison, the dissolved gas represents:
options: The gases dissolved in magma, which drive the eruption when they try to escape
The lava that flows down the slope
The ash that falls on nearby farms
The rock of the crater walls

questions.question: Magma described as 'cold, stiff pap that plugs its own pipe' will produce:
options: A gentle, effusive eruption of long lava flows
A violent, explosive eruption of ash, cinders and volcanic bombs
No eruption of any kind
A hot spring only

questions.question: The main control on how runny or thick a magma is:
options: Its depth below the surface
The age of the volcano
Its silica content
The width of the vent

questions.question: The 'pancake' volcano in the lesson is the:
options: Composite volcano
Shield volcano — wide, low and gently sloping
Cinder cone
Dome volcano

questions.question: In the layer-cake comparison, the 'icing that holds the crumbs down' stands for:
options: The magma chamber
The parasitic cone
The lava layer that seals each ash layer in place
The crater rim

questions.question: Working from the bottom up, the plumbing of a volcano is:
options: Crater, vent, magma chamber
Vent, magma chamber, crater
Caldera, crater, vent
Magma chamber, vent, crater

questions.question: Ngorongoro in Tanzania, a huge basin many kilometres across with a wildlife-filled floor, formed when:
options: A giant eruption emptied the magma chamber and the unsupported summit collapsed inward
A river eroded the top of a shield volcano
Two plates pulled apart along a transform fault
A dolerite sill was exposed by weathering

questions.question: The skyline of the Drakensberg is a wall of flat steps and ramparts rather than pointed peaks because:
options: It was carved by glaciers
It is built of stacked basalt lava sheets erupted from long fissures
It is a row of eroded composite cones
It is a single vast caldera rim

questions.question: Kimberlite pipes at Kimberley and Cullinan are important because they:
options: Produced the Karoo dolerite sills
Formed the Bushveld platinum reserves
Blasted up from the mantle carrying diamonds with them
Are still actively erupting

questions.question: Which pairing of benefit and place is CORRECT?
options: Geothermal electricity — Kimberley
Platinum and chromium — the Drakensberg
Diamonds — Marion Island
Geothermal energy — Iceland and Kenya's Rift Valley

questions.question: The four-step approach to managing a volcanic hazard given in the lesson is:
options: Watch the instruments, map the danger zones, plan settlement and evacuation, practise the drill
Predict the date, evacuate, rebuild, insure
Drill the vent, cool the lava, divert the ash, replant
Measure the magnitude, rank the intensity, count the damage, claim
